subject: Specifying priors on Intercept and Slope mean in LGCM

messages.author: f6d77eeabf5acd39
messages.subject: Specifying priors on Intercept and Slope mean in LGCM
parts:
Hi all,

 

I’m running a Bayesian latent growth model, and I would like to check whether I have specified the priors in the correct way.  

 

I have specified the (blavaan default) priors for mean of the Intercept and Slope as follows:

i ~ prior("dnorm(0, 0.001)") * 1 

s ~ prior("dnorm(0, 0.001)") * 1

 

However, when I specify the priors like this, the prior distributions of other parameters in the model change...

For example, the Wishart distribution of the Covariance Int & Slope changes into a beta distribution, and the variances of the Intercept and Slope become a gamma distribution instead of a Wishart (looks like they are treated as residual variances)...


Does anyone know how these priors should be specified?
 

Best,

Sanne

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Specifying priors on Intercept and Slope mean in LGCM
parts:
Sanne,

In jags, it can be helpful to jointly put an inverse wishart on variance/covariance parameters associated with latent variables. However, when you start to put custom priors on latent variable parameters, it can become impossible to use an inverse wishart. So blavaan checks whether you are using your own custom priors on latent variable parameters, then decides what to do about this prior.

The blavaan paper has lots of detail on custom specification of these priors. Basically, if you don't use an inverse wishart, you can write each covariance as the product of a correlation and two standard deviations. Then the priors go on the correlation (beta) and associated variances (inverse gamma).

Either of these specifications (inverse wishart or correlation/variances) is valid. The sampling under inverse wishart might be a little more efficient, but it will not make a major difference in many situations.

Best,
Ed

Hi Ed (and anyone else who is reading),

I am also interested in specifying a custom prior for an Intercept and Slope mean. After reading your reply here, I would like to try to also specify a custom inverse Wishart prior to see if it is possible to overide the Blavaan "instinct" to switch to beta/inverse gamma priors (this all to replicate an analysis done in a different software package). I was wondering how I could also specify this custom prior on the inverse Wishart prior? In your publication you write:

"The default prior on blocks of precision parameters is the Wishart with identity scale matrix and degrees of freedom equal to the dimension of the scale matrix plus one. The user cannot easily make changes to this prior distribution via the dp argument. Changes can be made, however, by exporting the JAGS syntax and manually editing it. This is further described in the next section."

But how would one do this in the JAGS syntax? I've tried to find a relevant example in the documentation about JAGS but I am coming up empty handed so far.

Thank you for any help/direction you can provide!

Best,
Sonja

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Specifying priors on Intercept and Slope mean in LGCM
parts:
Sonja,

In the blavaan paper (url below), there is an "extensions of jags syntax" section that shows how to modify the underlying jags code.

https://arxiv.org/pdf/1511.05604.pdf

I think you would start by not changing the priors in your model, then export jags code, then find the part that assigns a wishart prior (part of the line will look like " ~ dwish(iden, 3)"). Then change the wishart parameters.

Also, if you just want to change the df parameter of the wishart, then you might have luck adding the following argument to your bsem/bcfa/blavaan command:

dp = dpriors(ibpsi="dwish(iden,10)")

where 10 is your desired degrees of freedom (but I haven't tested this to know for sure).

Finally, if you are looking to match default mplus priors, you won't be able to do it because jags does not allow for improper priors (like gamma or wishart distributions with negative parameters).

Ed
